name: Open Bandit Dataset
description: Off-policy evaluation (OPE) aims to estimate the performance of hypothetical policies using data generated by a different policy. Because of its huge potential impact in practice, there has been growing research interest in this field. There is, however, no real-world public dataset that enables the evaluation of OPE, making its experimental studies unrealistic and irreproducible. With the goal of enabling realistic and reproducible OPE research, we present Open Bandit Dataset, a public logged bandit dataset collected on a large-scale fashion e-commerce platform, ZOZOTOWN. Our dataset is unique in that it contains a set of multiple logged bandit datasets collected by running different policies on the same platform. This enables experimental comparisons of different OPE estimators for the first time. We also develop Python software called Open Bandit Pipeline to streamline and standardize the implementation of batch bandit algorithms and OPE. Our open data and software will contribute to fair and transparent OPE research and help the community identify fruitful research directions. We provide extensive benchmark experiments of existing OPE estimators using our dataset and software. The results open up essential challenges and new avenues for future OPE research.
evaluation_method: estimated policy value (average reward) and estimator error (e.g., MSE of estimated policy value)
general_score_metric: estimated policy value (expected reward) and OPE estimator MSE
reputation: Widely cited and adopted in the bandits/OPE research community as a large-scale, real-world logged bandit dataset enabling reproducible OPE experiments.
notes: Real-world logged bandit data from an e-commerce platform — strong realism but domain-specific; contains multiple logging policies enabling multi-policy comparisons; not an LLM benchmark and care needed for selection bias and covariate shift.
